page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, AES cryptography, and FMA. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.hfc7.6xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with a notable exception in memory performance. The PassMark memory score is classified as strong, placing in the top 25% of tested systems, supported by a read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 1393.48 GB/sec. CPU-bound benchmarks show a Geekbench multi-core score of 10393.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 25430.3. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 18.51 GB/sec and processes Redis SET operations at 23.87 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds on a medium 7B model reach 35.74 tokens per second for prompt processing and 12.11 tokens per second for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed make this instance a solid choice for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio optimizes resource allocation for applications where CPU performance is the primary bottleneck. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes over the baseline 8 Gbps network interface. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, database operations, and moderate-scale CPU-based machine learning inference.
